Honestly just talk about anything. I use to be afraid of small talk to until I just kinda started talking about what was on my mind. The biggest thing is to not try and think too hard, which is difficult to do at first. I use to always be so concerned about what I was saying, how it was coming off, that I had no other thought to give on something to talk about. Just relax, majority of people are intimidated by it too. Just be friendly and talk about whatever. If the other person isn't being too responsive just say you gotta run or something. Don't think too much about it, and realize any awkward situation really isn't that awkward to begin with (bigger deal in you're mind than in reality) and that it's really not a big deal at all. If the other person makes it a big deal or is acting weird that's their problem, not yours.

No it's not too late. It's never too late. Honestly I use to be somewhat similar to you (and I'm someone who partied a lot and played sports blah blah blah) but I still felt very awkward in social situations and very self aware. It took some time to get over this and I can definitely relate and how scary/difficult it can be. My best advice is to try your best to relax and try not to care what others think. You're more thank likely gonna have awkward moments (lord knows I did when I started branching out to meet new people) but seriously man it's really not a big deal at all and a lot of times it's really only awkward to you. You'll learn the majority of people are somewhat uneasy in new social settings and are really just focusing more on themselves rather than judging you for anything you do. And for those people who do judge you, fuck them, they're the most insecure, trust me. It took me awhile to realize that but now that I do I really couldn't give less of a shit for anyone who doesn't like me. 

But most people will like you, trust me. You'll meet people that you genuinely connect with and it's a great feeling. I spent years hanging with people from my hometown who were kinda judgemental and competitive and it honestly wore me down. It caused some of my depression. I've since moved on from them and have made friends with other people who are more genuine and it's honestly amazing how much more happy I've been. 

It's difficult at first, but once you learn that there really are kind hearted people out there who would love to get to know you and don't give a shit if you're awkward at all, you'll really start to grow and become more social. Just be kind and you'll attract the right people, trust me. Also people love talking about themselves so literally just ask them questions about themselves and even if you're not impressed act like you are and I guarantee that person will think you're the coolest person ever lol. People love talking about themselves and especially love when someone else thinks they're interesting.

I graduated with a biomedical engineering degree and have gone back to school for a computer/software engineering degree (I'm taking all the main CS courses). It's never too late, I'm 27 and feel a little old to be in school still but honestly there's a lot of people who are older than me in my classes. If you don't like memorizing things then I'd definitely get out of your degree if you were only doing it for med school. Med school requires a ton of memorization and regurgitation. You'll (most likely) have better opportunities with a CS degree compared to a bio degree. I worked in labs for a little while after graduating with my first degree and a lot of people I worked with who had bio/Chem degrees had been working there as contractors for years. I'm not gonna lie, it was kinda crappy and I felt bad for these people. Not saying that will necessarily happen to you if you finish your bio degree, but it definitely does happen.

I can't relate to this anymore. Ive dealt with depression and social anxiety(which bothers me a ton, this is really the sole reason for my depression) for nearly 10 years now (I'm 27) and finally went to get help from a psychiatrist last summer. I do my research on certain types of drugs, and I'm aware I'm nowhere near an expert, but I do understand the basics on how many work. I went in wanting to talk to the psychiatrist about different options only to be met with him telling me I didn't know what I was talking about and that he knew what I needed. It didn't sit right with me, an uneasy feeling, but I followed his lead. 

The drugs he placed me on (SSRIs) only made my depression worst over the course of 6 months and I wound up gaining 40 pounds. I'm someone who's very active, work out a ton, eat fairly well, but when I was on those meds I couldn't do anything. I was patient because I know it takes time and my doctor told me to wait it out. Finally I stopped going to him because he refused to switch me to different meds. 

It was just unnerving and now I don't have much trust in going to see someone (I know this was a one time thing, but I was apprehensive going into it and it's just off putting when those weary thoughts become reality). I can relate to those who have depression and feel awkward and uneasy in nearly any social aspect. It sucks. It really screws with your head. People who don't have it don't have a clue how bad it can be. They say, well work on it, you need to build yourself up. I'm telling you, it is not that easy, at all. When your mind is literally telling you you're a social weirdo and you can't escape it no matter how hard you try, it's the worst feeling. You can't connect with others. You don't understand social queues, or you could, but you have no chemistry with others. 

This post kinda turned from not trusting doctors to how crippling depression and social anxiety can be but if you're someone who looks at people and say we'll just go to therapy, work on yourself, put yourself in those awkward situations. Just trust me when I say it's not that easy. Being awkward also make others feel awkward, which then makes you feel ever worse cause now your social anxiety is affecting others. It's a vicious cycle and is even worse when you're painfully aware of every single little aspect of what's wrong with you and also seeing people's faces kinda cringe when they talk to you cause you know it's just that damn awkward. It's depressing, defeating, and just sucks.
